# Indie Market Report — November 2026

*Window: ~Oct 4 – Nov 3, 2026. Generated by an automated web-research run.*

## Read this first: data quality

- Most numbers are **developer-announced or press-reported, not verified** against SteamDB/Gamalytic. Sources conflict (noted per game). Several results came from low-quality aggregators; I leaned on them only where nothing better existed.
- **Honest finding:** the 30-day window produced *no brand-new sub-$20 small-team mega-hit*. The giants of the period (How to Fish, Meccha Chameleon) launched Aug/June and kept making headlines. October's new releases from small teams mostly priced at **$20–25**, outside your filter. I flag those separately rather than pad the list.
- Team sizes and marketing details are frequently **not reported**; I say "unknown" instead of guessing.
- "Past 30 days" for the first two entries means *traction/milestone news*, not launch date.

---

## 1. How to Fish — Dazed Games (Sweden)
- **Genre / platform / price:** Chaotic co-op fishing sandbox ("friendslop"); Steam. $7.99, launched Aug 20 at $4.95 intro discount (ended Aug 27).
- **Numbers:** Dev announced **10M players** (Oct 12) in <2 months. 1M in ~2 days; peak **370,901 CCU** (Aug 25). Some outlets call it copies sold; one claims 6.3M Steam units / ~$26M gross in August alone (inconsistent, unverified). Heavy China share (~30% of buyers per Gamalytic via a Russian report).
- **Why it worked:**
  - Simple loop (catch → sell → upgrade) that escalates into physics, trick shots, gambling, weapons, bosses. Players learn rules fast, then break them, producing unscripted, clippable moments.
  - **~$5 price = group impulse buy.** Friends buy together without deliberation.
  - Patch 1.0.4 raised lobbies 4 → 8 players; later private sessions. Fast live-ops on the viral wave.
- **Marketing:** Mixed accounts. One (Chinese-language, secondary) says the founders' first game flopped, so they made marketing central: dev videos on TikTok/Instagram, ~1,300-member Discord pre-launch. Another says no formal campaign. Landfall-backed (project funding) per GameDiscoverCo. **Verdict: strategy-seeded, then virality took over.**
- **Solo-replicable:** Short-form dev clips + a small Discord before launch; design for emergent, clippable chaos; price so friends can buy in a group chat; ship lobby-size/private-session fixes within days.
- **Red flags:** No published roadmap; unclear retention past launch surge; "players" vs "copies" ambiguity; server/lobby limits at launch (hence the patch).

## 2. Meccha Chameleon — lemorion_1224 + Haganeiro (Japan, 2 people)
- **Genre / platform / price:** Hide-and-seek paint-and-camouflage co-op; Steam; $5.99 (one source $4.79).
- **Numbers:** Launched Jun 9/10. 2M in 5 days, 15M in 25 days, **20M in 63 days** (dev-announced). Self-published.
- **Why it worked:** Instantly legible premise, funny failure moments, social/party play, rock-bottom price. Players recreating art (e.g., Mona Lisa) generated organic content.
- **Marketing:** Press repeatedly says near-zero marketing: streamers/clips plus word of mouth. "Zero spend" is an outlet claim, not confirmed.
- **Solo-replicable:** The *design* (streamable, shareable, cheap, co-op). Not replicable: the luck of the streamer pickup. Treat as a lottery ticket you improve odds on, not a plan.
- **Red flags:** Survivorship bias — the same formula (cheap co-op friendslop) is now crowded; sales figures are units, not revenue (heavy discounting/regional pricing likely).

## 3. CRACK — Rafoli (appears solo/very small; unconfirmed)
- **Genre / platform / price:** 1–4 player incremental co-op lab sim (crack a giant egg); Steam; ~$7.99 (one guide; other source said price unannounced at Oct 15). Released **Oct 26**.
- **Numbers:** No sales reported. Steam shows **Very Positive, ~1,482 reviews** within the week (GamingOnLinux roundup) — strong for a week-one indie at this price.
- **Why it worked (inferred):** Co-op incremental = low-friction, high-chatter genre; division of labor between players (one cracks the egg, another sells shells) creates natural communication and clips.
- **Marketing:** Documented development publicly on social media; dev quote: *"Half the game's best ideas came from comments under my videos."* Build-in-public video loop doing both marketing and design feedback.
- **Solo-replicable:** Highly. Short videos → comments → features → launch audience. Cheapest strategy in this report.
- **Red flags:** Each co-op player needs their own copy (friction); no hard sales data; review-score hype on a short window can decay.

## 4. Queen's Domain — Freshly Baked Games (duo; published by Future Friends Games)
- **Genre / platform / price:** Retro first-person fantasy action RPG (King's Field-style); PC, PS5, Xbox, Switch 2. **$19.99** (15% launch discount). Released **Oct 30**.
- **Numbers:** Steam **Overwhelmingly Positive, ~1,185 reviews** within days. Sales unknown. Pre-launch: ~50,000 wishlists in a week after announcement (GamesRadar headline).
- **Why it worked:** Tight niche (King's Field/old FromSoft lineage) with almost no modern competition; **free demo live since Dec 2025 with 850+ Very Positive reviews** — nearly 11 months of demo-driven word of mouth.
- **Marketing:** Demo-first, niche-press coverage (RPG Site, PCGamesN, GamesRadar), publisher for console ports. Note: one outlet called it solo; most say duo.
- **Solo-replicable:** Long-lived public demo + a sharply defined nostalgic niche. Less replicable: publisher/console launch.
- **Red flags:** $19.99 sits on your price ceiling; publisher deal means revenue share; niche caps the ceiling.

## 5. Tape to Tape — Excellent Rectangle (Canada, 3 co-founders)
- **Genre / platform / price:** Roguelite hockey; Steam/consoles; ~£16.75 UK (US price not confirmed). 1.0/full release reported **Oct 23, 2026**; **Very Positive, ~3,719 reviews**.
- **Numbers:** Not an October launch. Early Access began May 2023: 34,020 units / ~$636K gross in 8 days with 53K launch wishlists (Chris Zukowski breakdown). No 2026 figures found.
- **Why it worked:** Sports × roguelite synergy-building is an underserved mashup; streamer Northernlion support; Kickstarter (CA$46.7K, May 2022) proved demand first.
- **Marketing:** Kickstarter → Next Fest → social posts → Northernlion. Paid ads reportedly underperformed.
- **Solo-replicable:** Kickstarter as validation; Next Fest; courting one aligned mid-size streamer rather than many. Early Access runway of ~3 years is *not* a solo-friendly timeline.
- **Red flags:** Long dev cycle; uncertain whether 1.0 sales are strong (no data).

## 6. REKA — Emberstorm Entertainment (published by Fireshine Games)
- **Genre / platform / price:** Cozy witch/walking-cottage sandbox; Steam; $19.99 (35% launch discount to Nov 7). 1.0 reported Oct 26 (dates conflict: one source said Aug 18).
- **Numbers:** ~2,000 reviews; 83–"Very Positive" (sources differ). No sales numbers found.
- **Why it worked:** Distinctive Slavic-folklore hook; ~2 years of Early Access; Rhianna Pratchett attached as lead writer (press-friendly).
- **Marketing:** Publisher-led, seasonal content (Halloween updates), launch discount.
- **Solo-replicable:** Seasonal event content + long Early Access feedback loop. Writer/name-attachment is budget-dependent.
- **Red flags:** Team size unknown; publisher-backed, so a weak model for a solo dev; 1.0 date confusion.

## Noted but excluded (over $20, or free/not indie-small)
| Game | Why excluded / note |
|---|---|
| **Silver Pines** (Wych Elm, 5 people, Team17) | Fits team size, but ~$24.99. 100K+ sold in the first week (Oct 8 → Oct 15); 95% positive. Worth studying: long Lynchian/Twin Peaks aesthetic hook and demo. |
| **over the hill** (Funselektor) | $24.99; 94% of ~3,200 reviews positive; follow-up to *art of rally*; multi-channel social presence. |
| **SULFUR** (Perfect Random, Sweden) | $24.99→$29.99 at 1.0 (Oct 28); 200K+ copies in Early Access (another report: 500K). Multiplayer unlocked at 200K — a smart community-milestone mechanic. |
| **Order of the Sinking Star** | Jonathan Blow; >$20. |
| **Cucina Stellata** | Free. Overwhelmingly Positive (~977). Short horror — a pure reputation play. |

## Cross-cutting patterns
1. **$5–$8 + co-op + clippable chaos** is the dominant viral formula of 2026 (How to Fish, Meccha Chameleon, CRACK). It is also getting crowded.
2. **Public build + comments → features** (CRACK) is the lowest-cost, most solo-friendly marketing loop here.
3. **Niche + long-running free demo** (Queen's Domain) beats a Next Fest spike. Next Fest median is only ~806 wishlists per participating demo; it amplifies existing momentum rather than creating it.
4. **Wishlist benchmarks:** first-week sales ≈ 10–20% of launch wishlists; ≈ 0.10× for games above $10 (GameDiscoverCo).
5. **Live-ops speed matters:** lobby/size patches within days kept the viral wave from stalling.

## Gaps / what I could not verify
- No confirmed sales for CRACK, Queen's Domain, Tape to Tape (2026), or REKA 1.0.
- Team sizes for CRACK, REKA, and Tape to Tape's current lineup are not confirmed.
- October Next Fest (Oct 19–26) breakout wishlist numbers weren't published in anything I found.
- Recommended follow-up: pull Gamalytic/SteamDB for the titles above before acting on any figure.
